scope: Proposition 5.5 (Uniform expanding-torus transfer) of the manuscript “Stable self-similar blowup for a supercritical defocusing Schrödinger equation on the torus” (preprints/Stable-Self-Similar-Blowup-for-a-Supercritical-Defocusing-Schrodinger-Equation-on-the-Torus-September-24-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 371 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 09887025fcf67354), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 42. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: For each fixed M > 0 the step maps F (M) L are uniformly bounded for all sufficiently large L. Writing L′ = LeM/2, lim L→∞ ∥πL′ F (M) L − eMΛ πL∥L(YL,R14) = 0. (5.27) There exists M0 < ∞ such that for every fixed M ≥ M0 there is L0(M) < ∞ for which ∥(I − PL′ )F (M) L |ker πL ∥L(YL,YL′ ) ≤ 1 8 , L ≥ L0(M). (5.28) Moreover ∥(I − PL′ )F (M) L EL∥ ≤ CM . Any prescribed positive bound on the coordinate defect can be imposed by enlarging L0(M) after M has been fixed. These bounds persist after restarting a step at any larger scale. After identifying torus spaces by dilation, the maps above and the step propagator are continuous when the scale and the input vary continuously. This last assertion is strong continuity for varying inputs, and does not assert operator-norm continuity of Schrödinger time evolution.
